    Rendering, Updating and Sharing

    Last updated on 2026-11-19 | Edit this page

    Overview

    Questions

    • How do you turn your dashboard into a file that colleagues can open?
    • How do you update the dashboard when new data arrives?
    • Where can you go from here?

    Objectives

    • Render the dashboard to a single, shareable HTML file
    • Update the dashboard with new data or for a different institution by changing one line
    • Name next steps for extending your OA dashboard

    Rendering the dashboard

    Every time you click Render in RStudio, Quarto runs all the code in your document from top to bottom and writes a file named after your document with the .html extension, into your project folder. Open it with a double click: it works in any web browser, and the interactive table work without R or RStudio.

    By default, Quarto also creates a folder (filename_files) with supporting files that the HTML file needs. To share the dashboard as one self-contained file, for example as an e-mail attachment or on an intranet page, add one more setting to the YAML header:

    YAML 

    ---
title: "Open Access Monitoring Dashboard"
format:
  dashboard:
    theme: morph
    logo: images/lc_logo.svg
    embed-resources: true
---

    Render again. The resulting dashboard file now contains everything it needs.

    Updating the dashboard

    This is where a code-based dashboard pays off. Imagine a new data export arrives next quarter:

    1. Save the new CSV in the data folder (with the same file name, or adapt the file name in the setup chunk)
    2. Click Render

    That is all. Every value box, chart and table is recalculated. To produce the dashboard for another institution, change my_ror in the setup chunk and render.

    Challenge

    Challenge: One dashboard, two institutions

    Your library supports a partner institution and wants to compare. Change my_ror in the setup chunk of your dashboard to a different institution’s ROR ID (from the count() output in the data episode) and render again.

    1. What changed on the dashboard? What stayed the same?
    2. Which indicators would you want to put next to each other to compare the two institutions?

    Sharing your dashboard

    There are several ways to share a dashboard, from simple to more involved:

    • send the single HTML file by e-mail or put it on a shared drive or intranet page
    • publish it on Quarto Pub or GitHub Pages
    • use your institution’s web server or an institutional publishing platform

    See the Quarto publishing documentation for details.

    Where to go from here

    You now have all the building blocks of a Quarto dashboard. Natural next steps:

    • add a sidebar and tabsets to organise more content (see the Quarto layout documentation)
    • add more OA indicators, such as the share of articles covered by a transformative agreement (!is.na(esac_id)), or APC spending if you have cost data
    • fetch your own data directly from open sources such as OpenAlex instead of working with a CSV file
    • look at the Quarto dashboard gallery for ideas
    • continue with other Library Carpentry lessons

    Key Points

    • Render runs all code and writes an HTML file; embed-resources: true makes it a single shareable file
    • To update the dashboard, replace the data and render again; to change the institution, change the ROR ID in my_ror
    • A dashboard can be shared as a single HTML file, or published on Quarto Pub or GitHub Pages
